sources.entry: Identity management (IdM), also known as identity and access management (IAM or IdAM), is a framework of policies and technologies to ensure that the right users have the appropriate access to technology resources.

summary.name: Identity and access management
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia overview of identity and access management (IAM/IdM), a framework of policies and technologies that ensures the right users have appropriate access to technology resources.
use_cases: Controlling which employees can access company applications
Setting up single sign-on across services
summary.what_it_does: The page explains identity and access management as a framework covering how users gain identities, how those identities are authenticated, and what roles, permissions and entitlements they hold. It describes five functions: identity creation and deletion, user log-on, service delivery, identity federation and auditing. It covers federation via identity providers and service providers using SAML assertions, and lists system capabilities such as authentication, authorization, roles, delegation and interchange. It also surveys related standards (ISO/IEC 24760, SAML 2.0, OAuth, OpenID, NIST SP 800-63) and privacy considerations.
notable: Describes the configuration and operation phases of IAM and the split between identity management and access management
Covers identity federation with identity provider and service provider roles and SAML assertions
Lists related ISO/IEC standards and protocols such as SAML, OAuth, OpenID and Shibboleth
caveats: Encyclopedic overview, not a software product; no tool is described as downloadable or installable
Some sections are generic and cite external sources; several references are dated (e.g., EU projects from 2007-2013)
